recipes.name: Chicken and Dressing Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) package herb-seasoned dry bread stuffing mix
1 (4 pound) whole chicken, deboned and cut into bite size pieces
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of celery soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix butter, stuffing mix, and sage in a medium bowl until combined; spread mixture on the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spread cooked chicken over mixture. Combine cream of chicken soup, cream of celery soup, and water until blended; pour over chicken.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbling and golden on top, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Dressing Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This chicken and dressing casserole made with cooked chicken and cornbread stuffing in a creamy sauce tastes just like a stuffed roast chicken.

review.reviewBody: This was a delicious recipe. Only thing I didn't like was that the dressing was not moist. So next time I will add 1 can of chicken broth to the dressing, butter and sage. I added 2 cups milk to soup mixture and no water. This makes a thicker gravy-type consistency.

I love this recipe idea and also tweaked it some. I only used one can of soup (cream of chicken) and one can of milk. I sauteed onions in the butter for the stuffing and used Stove Top stuffing mix. I reserved about one-third of the stuffing mixture and put it on the top before baking. The casserole was very, very good--almost custardy in texture but crispy on top, yummy! Made lots of leftovers to freeze for a single gal, too, and it reheated well in microwave and oven!

I had cut up & froze a Costco rotisserie chicken & was looking for an easy dinner receipe & this one caught my eye. Took chicken out & unthawed & drained any water off. I followed the receipe exactly except my Stovetop Dressing was the extra sage kind so I didn't add any other sage. I did slice up fresh baby bella mushrooms & put on top of the chicken. I baked this for 50 minutes, took out of oven & sprinkled mozzarella cheese on top & put back in oven for 10 minutes. Took out & let set for 5 minutes before serving. All the way through dinner my husband kept saying "OMG this is sooo good! It tastes like having your Thanksgiving dinner...this would be good on a cold winters night". With that feedback I will definitely make this again!!!

I changed the recipe a bit by following the suggestions of other reviewers. I sauteed onions and celery in the butter and seasoned them with Lawry's Seasoned Salt and fresh cracked pepper. I added 1/2 can of Swanson's chicken broth to the stuffing mix. In another bowl I mixed the chicken pieces with 1 can Cream of Chicken and 1 can of regular whole milk, omitting the Cream of Celery. I then poured over the stuffing mix and baked it for 45 minutes. We enjoyed this dish and it does remind us of Thanksgiving dinner.

I made several minor changes to accommodate what I had on hand and it was great. I cut up the chicken breasts, fried them in olive oil and then shredded them. I used Stove Top for the dressing and since a half cup of butter seemed like too much for the stuffing amount, I nearly doubled the stuffing. I didn't have sage, so I used celery salt. I t was slightly salty, but not really overly. I only used one can of cream of chicken soup, and instead of water, I used the broth from a can of chicken noodle soup and dumped the noodles in the compost. It was plenty of liquid. I mixed it all together and topped it with dried bread crumbs. I only needed to bake it for 30 minutes and served it with cranberry sauce . I'll make this again. We loved it. OK. I just made this a second time and I am NOT going to use the celery salt again! It really makes it too salty. Just leave it out or use the original seasoning!

I used a can of cream of chicken on the dressing then layered the chicken then another can cream of chicken soup. Baked for 35 minutes on 350°. Added mashed potatoes and green beans as sides delicious.

My family really enjoyed this tonight. I didn’t have cream of celery so I substituted cream of mushroom and used half of the water. I baked as directed for the first thirty minutes but then I mixed it together so the stuffing wouldn’t be dry. I then baked it for another twenty minutes. I served it with cranberry sauce. I think next time I will mix in some broccoli for a complete meal.
Delicious BUT I added a can of chicken broth to the dressing & a sautéed onion. Cut the butter in half. My picky eaters gobbled it up!

I loved this but I made a good amount of alterations. Instead of herb dressing I use cornbread. Also I mix the cornbread dressing with chicken stock and sauteed onions in butter until moist. Then I layer with a bag of mixed frozen veggies. I top that with cooked shredded chicken and then cover with a mix of 1 can cream of mushroom, 1 can cream of celery, and one can cream of chicken. Top it off with bread crumbs and bake. It barely fits in the 9x13 pan but it is soo good! We love it.

I made this and loved it, the few changes I made were to use chicken broth instead of water. I also doubled the cream of chicken with no cream of celery. I used celery salt instead.
It's great!

Yummy! I added half a cup of chicken broth to the stuffing mixture. Also, did half the water it asked and the rest chicken broth for more flavor. It turned out a little too soupy for our liking so next time I'll add another 6oz. box of stuffing mix.

Growing up, things were different, food was different. My mom would make the very BEST Chicken and dressing casserole for dinner and that meal never left my head, my heart or my tummy. Even though she's not here anymore, she lives through this for sure. Another meal my grandmother made, was her spaghetti, she baked it, after she would brown the ground beef, she would make the pasta sauce and let them cook together on the stove in a pot, with lots of Italian seasoning and then she'd mix the cooked noodles in with the meat sauce and bake it. NOBODY ever made spaghetti like her that I've ever had since then. Not even close.
Cooked longer

I listened to the reviews that said it was too dry and added half a can of chicken broth. I ended up cooking it for an hour longer than the recipe called for and at a higher temperature and it was still very soupy. We replaced the cream of chicken soup with cream of mushroom and added an onions as well. Overall it tasted fine I was just disappointed that I listened to the reviews that said it was too dry because it honestly ruined the dish

I doubled the dressing. Used 1 1/2 cups water, 1 1/2 cups chicken broth. Using another reviewer's suggestion and added sliced mushrooms over chicken. Baked 45 min and sprinkled motzarella over top. Baked another 15 min. Let sit 15 min. Really good!
added more seasoning
It's great 👍
This is my to go to last 2 years so good I just leave the water out and add chicken broth and add celery so yummy
We loved this! I first thought it was going to be too soupy on the top but I cooked it a bit longer. The leftovers were even better! We will definitely make this again
Loved this!! So easy to make, and a great casserole to bring to others!!
